research_caveat: IMPORTANT: no Groq page could be fetched directly this session. WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for every URL attempted (groq.com/privacy-policy, groq.com/security, trust.groq.com, console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-data-processing-addendum), and the sandbox egress proxy denied direct curl CONNECTs to console.groq.com outright (confirmed via the agent-proxy status endpoint: 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)'; WebFetch also 403'd on example.com, i.e. all direct fetching is blocked in this environment, not just Groq). Every value below is sourced from Groq's OWN pages (groq.com, console.groq.com, trust.groq.com) as quoted in web-search result excerpts. Per researcher hard rules ('confidence: high requires a URL you actually fetched'), confidence is capped at 'low' everywhere, even where the underlying vendor page is unambiguous. The web-search budget for the session was also exhausted mid-research, so the security-onboarding page and trust-center FAQ could not be probed further. The verifier pass should re-fetch each source_url from an unrestricted network (these pages load fine in a normal browser) before any value is promoted. Key unread primary sources that very likely answer the Not-known fields: https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-data-processing-addendum (DPA + TOM annex), https://console.groq.com/docs/production-readiness/security-onboarding, https://trust.groq.com/faq ('Security at Groq'), https://groq.com/security.

1.4.2.locator: Groq Trust Center (trust.groq.com; resources page at trust.groq.com/resources, FAQ 'Security at Groq' at trust.groq.com/faq). Groq's own materials state SOC 2 Type II compliance (maintained since mid-2024, current report available) and annual engagements of qualified, independent external auditors against recognized audit standards including SOC 2 Type II. The GroqCloud product page (https://groq.com/groqcloud) additionally states GroqCloud is 'SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant'.
1.4.2.notes: SOC 2 (Type II) is the only dropdown-listed certification confirmed from Groq-domain material this session. HIPAA compliance is claimed on the GroqCloud page and a Business Associate Addendum is published at https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-business-associate-addendum, but HIPAA is not an allowed dropdown value — noted here only. No ISO 27001/27701/27018/9001/22301, SOC 1, or SOC 3 claim was found on any Groq source. GATE: scope.yaml has soc2_on_file_in_vanta: null for Groq — per the playbook, do not assert SOC 2 in the form until Groq's SOC 2 Type II report is actually on file in Vanta; request it via trust.groq.com. Trust-center contents are gated/JS-rendered and could not be read this session.

3.1.1.locator: GroqDocs, Production Readiness > Security Onboarding: all Groq API traffic is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+; Groq APIs enforce HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher)
3.1.1.notes: Vendor's own security-onboarding documentation states 'TLS 1.2 or higher' is enforced, per search excerpts of the page (page itself unfetchable this session). 'TLS 1.2' is the honest dropdown floor; ask the vendor whether TLS 1.3 is preferred/negotiated on api.groq.com so the answer can be upgraded. Do not select TLS 1.3 without written confirmation.

3.1.2.notes: Groq's own documentation (security-onboarding page excerpt) states data at rest in production datastores is encrypted 'using strong encryption algorithms', but no Groq primary source retrieved this session names the standard (AES-128/192/256 etc.). 'Not known' is a valid dropdown option for this row. Searched: console.groq.com/docs/production-readiness/security-onboarding, trust.groq.com/faq, groq.com/security, console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-data-processing-addendum (all unfetchable; excerpts only), plus targeted queries for 'Groq AES-256 at rest backups key management' which returned nothing vendor-specific. The DPA's TOM annex and the gated trust center very likely name the algorithm — ask the vendor or read those once reachable.

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented in any Groq-domain material retrieved this session. Per the field playbook this is rarely documented separately and 'Not known' is common and correct. Ask the vendor which algorithm covers backups of systems holding customer prompt/transcript content, if any such backups exist (Groq's API data-retention posture should be confirmed in the same question).

3.1.4.notes: No Groq primary source retrieved this session describes key management, who generates encryption keys, or any CMEK/BYOK option. The playbook default for managed cloud ('Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)') is plausible but would be an industry-norm inference, which the hard rules forbid. Ask the vendor; also confirm with the human whether Tavus has any customer-managed-key arrangement with Groq (none is expected for a plain inference API).

3.1.6.notes: No Groq primary source retrieved this session states an anonymization capability over customer personal data. The DPA (console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-data-processing-addendum) governs processing of personal data in Customer Data but its text could not be read this session. Ask the vendor whether personal data contained in API inputs/outputs can be anonymized on the customer's instruction.

3.1.7.notes: No Groq primary source retrieved this session states a pseudonymization capability over customer personal data. Same situation as 3.1.6 — the unread DPA/TOM annex is the likely place this is answered. Ask the vendor.
